Samuel, saw Dazos raise its $25M Series A and ship iCampaign plus the RVK AI agent partnership.

Growth and a launch usually mean more in-market treatment centers in play than a sales team can cover before they cool, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Dazos off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Samuel, quick follow-up for Dazos.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually climb faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Dazos needs across behavioral health accounts this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Samuel, last bit of proof for Dazos.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Dazos' reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a behavioral health motion? I'll tailor it to Dazos either way.
